absent_because.max_decompressed_bytes: this adapter inflates nothing: a compressed response is unwrapped by the host under its own bounds before it is handed over
absent_because.max_parse_seconds: no wall-clock bound is enforced: this module reads no clock, and every pass is one walk of the document; a synthetic 3,000-item document translates in seconds (tests/test_cdm_frost_observations_adapter.py perf test), and the conformance suite's parser worker kills a decode that overruns its deadline

max_depth.enforced_at: `Adapter.__init_subclass__`'s wrapper calls `adapter.enforce_depth_bound` on the JSON text or the dict before this class's `to_cdm` runs
max_depth.source: A Frost response nests six containers (response, data, item, observations, observation, level). 64 (`MAX_DEPTH`) is the harness loader's own bound and the figure the JSON-reading adapters of synapse_cdm declare. This is an IMPLEMENTATION CAP and is NOT the format's normative maximum (the Frost API states none).

max_input_bytes.enforced_at: `Adapter.__init_subclass__` wraps this class's own `to_cdm` with `enforce_input_bound` at class-definition time, so the octets are measured and refused before this module decodes them
max_input_bytes.source: No Frost document states a maximum response size. The largest batch response observed outside this repository (about 2,900 data items for about 20 stations over one day) is about 3.5 MB; 16 MiB (16 777 216 octets, `MAX_INPUT_BYTES`, `adapters/frost_observations.py`) leaves four times that headroom. This is an IMPLEMENTATION CAP and is NOT the format's normative maximum (the Frost API states none).

max_objects.enforced_at: `FrostObservationsAdapter.to_cdm` counts the Events and the distinct stations after classifying every observation and before any object is built, and refuses `too-many-objects`
max_objects.source: One Event per data item and time class plus one Entity per station. A batch observed outside this repository is about 2,900 items for about 20 stations; 50 000 objects (`MAX_OBJECTS`) is about seventeen times that. This is an IMPLEMENTATION CAP and is NOT the format's normative maximum (the Frost API states none).

message_types: MET Norway Frost GET /observations/v0.jsonld ObservationResponse, one document per call, as its UTF-8 octets or its parsed dict; ENVIRONMENTAL_OBSERVATION Events carrying point-observation/1, one per data item (sourceId x referenceTime) and time class (instant, or Case 2.2 daily), and one SENSOR Entity per Frost station
capabilities.unknown_fields_basis: every Event's residual holds the response header (every top-level key but data) and its own data item verbatim, so a key this module does not know, at the top, in an item or in an observation, is carried under the format's namespace

format.name: MET Norway Frost ObservationResponse (GET /observations/v0.jsonld)
format.version: Frost API v0 (apiVersion "v0"), as documented at https://frost.met.no/concepts2.html

limitations.summary: only the observations/v0.jsonld ObservationResponse is translated; sources and elements responses are read only through the caller's StationTable and ElementTable, and no other Frost endpoint is read

the response states no position: a station's position comes only from the caller's StationTable keyed by the Frost station id (SN<n>); a station absent from it, or no table at all, gives an Entity with a null position and a position_basis saying so (the ndbc_stdmet/airnow_hourly precedent); masl and other SensorSystem fields are not carried

the parallel sensor number (the ':N' of sourceId) does not make an Entity of its own: the station is the identity, and the full sourceId is carried verbatim on each Event (contract station_id and source identifier) and listed on the station Entity

instant Events for sub-daily observations and for any referenceTime not at midnight; a separate Case 2.2 daily Event for P1D observations at midnight (period by timeOffset, observed_at its end); an observation at midnight with no timeResolution, one longer than P1D (monthly, seasonal, annual) or a P1D without a usable timeOffset gets no reading and is listed on the station Entity as unresolved; an instantaneous P1D value stored at exactly 00:00 would be read as diurnal, which the response cannot distinguish

the window a sub-daily elementId's calculation method names (sum(... PT1H)) is carried verbatim in the reading's name and not turned into an interval: validity.effective is the referenceTime instant, because the concepts page does not state where a sub-daily window lies relative to referenceTime

an observation without a unit takes the unit the caller's ElementTable names for its exact elementId, recorded as a transformation with the table's name; with no such row the reading is an Absence (unit_unknown) and the value stays only in the residual

timeOffset, timeResolution and timeSeriesId have no field in point-observation/1; they are stated verbatim in each reading's namespace (and in the residual), which is also what keeps two series of one element apart

because one item can make several Events (or none), the lossless ledger binds each item's leaves to the data_item residual of ANY Event, not to one object index; an item with no resolvable observation is carried in the station Entity's residual (unresolved_items), which the ledger does not bind
qualityCode, performanceCategory and exposureCategory are carried verbatim as typed quality flags and never interpreted into a confidence or a pass/fail; Event.quality is not set

the data licence is the response's own license statement (observed: CC BY 3.0 NO), carried verbatim; MET Norway's terms page names NLOD 2.0 and CC BY 4.0, and reconciling the two is the consumer's, not this module's
an observation without a numeric value is refused (bad-value): Frost publishes no sentinel for it, so there is no documented absence to translate

every fixture is synthetic (stations in the SN0000x block, positions inside CONTRIBUTING.md's Baltic rectangle, invented values) written from the documented response shape, which is what the gates ran against; no recorded Frost response is part of the evidence

the evidence RECORD for this adapter is not IN the distribution: `evidence/` is untracked and unpackaged, CI generates the set on every run, and the release pipeline generates the records for every shipped adapter and attaches them to the GitHub Release of the version it publishes. `evidence.available` is true because every published distribution that carries this adapter has that Release, so its records are retrievable by a third party; it says nothing about what the wheel contains

maturity.basis: L3 PROVENANCE VERIFIED, from evidence that runs today: `python -m synapse_cdm.harness --adapter frost_observations` reports translate, schema, provenance, lossless (basis: ledger, MAPPINGS declared, no LOST leaf) and golden PASS on every fixture. Every fixture is synthetic, written from the documented response shape and Frost's concepts page; the daily-at-midnight and missing-unit cases were found on real responses outside this repository, none of which is evidence here. L4 is NOT declared: the adapter is ingest-only, so the roundtrip check is inapplicable rather than passed, and a rung passed vacuously is not a rung declared.
